name: Dragon Radar
summary: A handheld tracker built by Bulma that points the way to the seven wish-granting Dragon Balls. Goku's whole adventure starts because she brought one to his mountain.

parts.label: Housing
parts.fact: Built by Bulma at sixteen after she found the Two-Star Ball in her family's basement. It debuted in the very first Dragon Ball chapter, printed in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1984.

parts.label: Signal source
parts.fact: Bulma built it after noticing that every Dragon Ball gives off a faint electromagnetic pulse; the radar simply listens for that pulse and plots where it comes from.

parts.label: Screen
parts.fact: The display shows each ball as a blip. Tuned for Earth's balls, it still worked on planet Namek, and a boosted Super Dragon Radar was later made by raising its sensitivity.

parts.label: Blind spots
parts.fact: It cannot pick up a ball that someone has swallowed, and Emperor Pilaf later came up with a box that hides a ball from the radar's scan.

parts.label: Copies & rebuilds
parts.fact: The original was stolen by the Red Ribbon Army and never recovered; a villager named Turbo copied it from airplane parts, and Bulma later rebuilt one from scratch.

trivia: Early English versions called it the Ball Detector or the Bleeper before Dragon Radar stuck.
Goku's radar broke during his fight with General White, and Bulma had to repair it.
Pilaf's gang built several rival radars, including one inside their ship with a big globe showing where the balls lay.
Bulma first meets Goku in that opening chapter, chasing the radar's signal straight to his grandfather's Four-Star Ball.
